description:
Surfaced during Arc 16 (CAPTAIN_PLINY → CAPTAIN_ZENO rename, stoa--kyg).
install.sh deploys role files + CAPTAIN envelopes by overwriting the
target paths, but does not remove files at the destination that are no
longer in the source. After Arc 16's rename + user-tier deploy, both
~/.claude/agents/CAPTAIN_PLINY.md (obsolete) and CAPTAIN_ZENO.md (current)
exist at user-tier — the PRINCIPAL has to manually rm the stale one.

Concrete next-step plan:
- Compare the deployed agents directory contents against the substrate's
  CAPTAIN_NAMES array
- Files in the deployed dir that match CAPTAIN_*.md (or
  CAPTAIN_*_<slug>.md in project mode) but whose mnemonic is not in
  CAPTAIN_NAMES → surface as candidates for removal
- Removal requires informed-consent gate (parallel to --modify-claude-md):
  default off; explicit --remove-stale flag enables it; --dry-run shows
  what would be removed
- Same logic applies to MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md / MAJOR_PLINY.md (less common,
  but the "rename of a MAJOR" case is parallel)
- Tier-aware: only operate on the deployed tier's directory, never reach
  into a different tier's

Blocker: none. This is a straightforward extension of install.sh that
needs design + implementation. Could be a small focused arc (Arc 17 or
later — out of the substrate-completeness sequence Arcs 16/17/18 already
queued).

Won't block any current work; the manual-deletion workaround is one rm
per rename. But this is the exact kind of fix-now-cost-near-zero gap the
fix-now discipline (§4.8) targets, so the ticket exists with a plan
rather than a handwave.
title: install.sh leaves obsolete deployed files in place after a rename
